clue.text: Returning painters are so talkative about this sea

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the painters' abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, the crossword's stock painters
talkative chatter is gas, idle talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some chatty artists on their way home discuss a particular sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses the painters; 'are' and 'about' only join the pieces, and 'this sea' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sargasso is the weed-choked sea of the North Atlantic, the one the clue points to as 'this sea'.

clue.text: Rising artist, ripe for a dynamic part?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
ripe fruit is mature, fully developed

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming painter is ready for an energetic role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns RA into AR. 'Dynamic' here means of a dynamo, not lively.
explanation.definitionFit: The armature is the rotating wound coil of a dynamo or motor, so a dynamo part.

clue.text: Defend one rag that creates an earthly paradise

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Protecting a scrap of cloth somehow brings heaven to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFENDONERAG is rearranged by 'that creates'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden in Genesis is the original paradise set on earth, home of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Was obviously apprehensive that one's timbers would be so treated?

definitions.text: that one's timbers would be so treated?

explanation.surface: Someone visibly nervous fears for the timbers of their ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old sailor's oath 'shiver my timbers', where to shiver is to smash to splinters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble visibly with fear is the first sense; to splinter wood is the second, as in the pirate's oath.

clue.text: One bloke's worried by the needle

indicators.note: worried means shaken about or harassed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the word is taken with its S

explanation.surface: A man is troubled by a sewing needle.
explanation.walkthrough: I and BLOKES, rearranged because of 'worried', give the answer. The needle is a stone pillar, as with Cleopatra's Needle in London, not a sewing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's Needle in London is an Egyptian stone pillar of this tapering kind, so 'needle' names one.

clue.text: Make speech without point but with embellishments

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the speech word goes round the point

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An orator drops the argument but keeps all the flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: ORATE goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is heavily decorated, full of flourishes and adornment.

clue.text: Narcotic effect for which many love the art master

parts.note: C, the Roman hundred, stands for many
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A drug's effect, for which many adore the painting master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art master' looks like a painter, but it is the degree MA, Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep stupor or unconsciousness is what a heavy narcotic dose brings on.

clue.text: A gallant ship's acts of retaliation

explanation.surface: A brave vessel carries out reprisals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Revenge was Sir Richard Grenville's ship, famous for its lone fight against a Spanish fleet in 1591.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenville's ship was named Revenge; acts of retaliation are paybacks for wrongs.

clue.text: Exclude one tone of voice

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leave out one note of the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singing voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Arabian caliph, namesake of Persian poet

explanation.surface: An Arab ruler shares his name with a Persian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second caliph of Islam bore the same first name as Khayyam, poet of the Rubaiyat.
explanation.definitionFit: The second caliph after Muhammad bore this name, as did Khayyam, author of the Rubaiyat.

clue.text: Possibility of Nick tending to be reckless?

parts.note: Old Nick is a name for the Devil
may expresses possibility, as in 'it may rain'
tending to someone is care

explanation.surface: Is the Devil likely to look after anyone, or is he too wild?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs DEVIL, MAY, CARE: 'of' places Nick ahead of the possibility word.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless attitude to risk is cavalier, heedless of what may happen.

clue.text: Holy orders

parts.note: looks like ordination of clergy, but read as orders given by God, the ten laid down to Moses

explanation.definitionFit: The ten given to Moses on Sinai are divine instructions, so sacred orders.

clue.text: Table-cloth smuggler ?

explanation.surface: A smuggler hides contraband under the tablecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A table runner is a long strip of cloth down a table; a gun-runner or rum-runner smuggles goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow cloth laid along a table is one sense; one who smuggles, as in rum-running, is the other.

clue.text: Wax lyrical about the side that's cooking

indicators.note: about means around, so the singing word surrounds the team

parts.note: to wax lyrical is to sing out praise
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses over the team that is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it is the container signal; 'that's' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Food steaming is being cooked over boiling water, so it is in the process of cooking.

clue.text: For which Albion was notorious

parts.note: the stock phrase 'perfidious Albion' pins treachery on England

explanation.definitionFit: Treachery and faithlessness were the vice foreigners pinned on England in 'perfidious Albion'.

clue.text: Banana weed

explanation.surface: A banana grows among the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a starchy cooking banana; the other a common broad-leaved garden weed of genus Plantago.

clue.text: Armed college men?

parts.note: the College of Arms is staffed by officers who deal with coats of arms, so its men are 'armed'

explanation.definitionFit: Officers of the College of Arms who devise and record coats of arms carry this title.

clue.text: Wordy appendage makes the client wild, I see ?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the word see sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: A grammatical appendage drives the customer wild, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CLIENT, I and C; 'makes the' joins. The letter C stands for 'see' because they sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclitic is a word attached to the one before it, like Latin -que, so an appendage to a word.

clue.text: Valley dweller gets his beer cheap !

explanation.surface: A countryman from the valleys drinks cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as D-ALES-MAN, a man whose ales cost a penny: D was the old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: One living in the Yorkshire Dales is a valley inhabitant; split up, he is a penny-ales man.

clue.text: A notice : "Variety of Monkshood"

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: A sign announces a kind of flowering plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges A NOTICE; it reads as part of the plant's description.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite is the poisonous plant also called wolfsbane, with hooded blue flowers.

clue.text: A century and a half century following Plato

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
demi- is a prefix meaning half
C again for the Roman hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty years of followers of Plato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A half century' looks like fifty, but it splits into A, DEMI and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato taught in the Academy, so his followers were Academics, of that school.

clue.text: What's Gray Owl doing? Work in China

indicators.note: in places the work inside the Chinese porcelain word

parts.note: Ming is the dynasty and its porcelain, so fine china
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks about an owl, then a job in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's Elegy speaks of 'the moping owl' complaining to the moon. China is the porcelain, MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Elegy says the owl is sullen and listless, brooding to the moon.

clue.text: Parboil cabbage about twopence

indicators.note: about means around, so the cabbage word goes round the pennies

parts.note: cole is an old word for cabbage, as in coleslaw
d was the abbreviation of the old penny, so twopence is two of them

explanation.surface: A recipe: half-boil the greens for a couple of coins.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the old British penny, from Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Coddle means to cook gently in water just below the boil, so to partly boil.

clue.text: Melodramatic situation of the Surrey side

explanation.surface: Something theatrical is going on south of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally 'across the bridges': the Surrey side is the south bank of the Thames, whose theatres were known for lurid melodrama.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatres over London's bridges staged sensational plays, so the word means both south-bank and lurid.

clue.text: Trouble in Laos as well?

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the country's letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Is there unrest in the South-East Asian country too?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble in' rearranges LAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Also is a plain synonym of too or in addition.

clue.text: A good one's not trash. Its loss could mean trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so the letters of mean are disturbed

explanation.surface: Losing one's good reputation could bring trouble, says the moralist.
explanation.walkthrough: From Iago in Othello: 'Who steals my purse steals trash... but he that filches from me my good name...'. 'Its loss could' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago sets reputation against the purse, which is trash, so a good reputation is the treasure.

clue.text: Imbued with natural impulse

explanation.surface: Filled with a natural urge.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective the answer means filled or charged, used with 'with': 'instinct with life'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective sense means filled or charged; the noun is an innate urge.

clue.text: For example about 91 do evil — should be cutting it out

indicators.note: about means around, so the example abbreviation wraps the rest

parts.note: XCI is 91 in Roman numerals
to sin is to do evil

explanation.surface: A moral warning: anyone doing evil should stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is the container signal; 91 as Roman numerals is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove by surgery, so this is cutting something away.
